damage_components.description: Entire windshield is spider-webbed with extensive cracking across the full surface. Multiple impact points visible. Not repairable.
Severely crumpled and buckled with visible deformation across the full panel. Creasing indicates structural deformation beyond panel beating.
Detached and hanging from the vehicle. Lower bumper section separated. Bumper cover and reinforcement both compromised.
Housing and surrounding mounting area crushed. Headlight likely non-functional due to structural intrusion.
Severe crush damage with panel pushed inward. Paint damage, panel deformation, and possible structural compromise to the inner guard.

damage_components.component: Front grille and Toyota badge surround
damage_components.description: Partially intact but misaligned due to bumper and hood displacement. Badge surround cracked.
Blue metallic paint required for all replaced panels. Colour matching and blending needed across bonnet, bumper, fender, and surrounding areas.

assessor_notes: Damage severity classified as Severe. Multiple structural and cosmetic components are affected. The extent of front-end crush damage, particularly to the driver-side fender and A-pillar area, raises concern about possible chassis or subframe damage that cannot be confirmed from a photograph alone. If structural inspection reveals chassis damage, the vehicle may be assessed as an economic total loss given the age and market value of a Toyota Corolla in this class. Emergency vehicles visible in background confirm this was a significant collision event. Cost estimates are indicative ranges based on Australian panel beating and parts pricing data retrieved via web lookup (source: Oneflare panel beating cost guide, April 2026). Individual quotes from authorised Toyota repairers may vary. Engine and mechanical damage cannot be assessed from external photographs.
